props.gloss_en: being unwitting only of the korban counts as shegaga (Munbaz); the Rabbis: it does not
R' Yochanan: once he was unwitting of the karet it is shegaga, though he knew the lav
Reish Lakish: it is not shegaga until he is unwitting of both the lav and the karet
the mishna: the primary labours are forty less one
R' Yochanan: if he did them all in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one
how can that be found? -- where he knew it was Shabbat and was unwitting of the labours
for R' Yochanan the case is found: he knew Shabbat as a lav [but not its karet]
for Reish Lakish: he knew [the law of] Shabbat boundaries, according to R' Akiva
unwitting of both [Shabbat and the labours] -- that is the unwitting sinner of the Torah
deliberate in both -- that is the deliberate sinner of the Torah
unwitting of Shabbat and deliberate in the labours, or unwitting of the labours and deliberate of Shabbat -- liable
or who said: I know this labour is forbidden, but not whether a korban is due for it -- liable
whose is this baraita? -- Munbaz's
Abaye: all agree that for an oath on a statement one is liable to a korban only if he was unwitting of its lav
'all agree' -- who [might have disagreed]? R' Yochanan
R' Yochanan spoke only where there is karet; here, where there is no karet, he did not
the korban for the oath is a novelty: nowhere else in the Torah do we find a lav for which one brings a korban, and here one does
you might have said: [because of the novelty] one unwitting only of the korban should also be liable
the baraita: what is an unwitting oath on the past? -- if he said 'I know this oath is forbidden, but not whether a korban is due' -- liable
whose is it? -- Munbaz's
rather, is it not the Rabbis'?

schemas.gloss_en: (for Munbaz) if throughout the Torah, where the korban is no novelty, being unwitting of the korban counts as shegaga, then for the oath on a statement, where it is a novelty, all the more so

supports.gloss_en: כי קאמר רבי יוחנן היכא דאיכא כרת -- R' Yochanan's leniency is confined to karet prohibitions, and the oath carries none

challenges.gloss_en: לישנא אחרינא: the baraita cannot be Munbaz's (that would be obvious a fortiori), so it is the Rabbis', and it refutes Abaye -- תיובתא

objections.gloss_en: the mishna's tally means liability for each labour, which requires Shabbat known and labours unwitting; for R' Yochanan he knew Shabbat as a lav, but for Reish Lakish, who needs him unwitting of the lav itself -- in what did he know Shabbat?

answered_by.gloss_en: דידעה בתחומין ואליבא דרבי עקיבא -- he knew the boundaries, which for R' Akiva are Torah law (= p_rl_yada_tchumin)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: one who knows the oath is forbidden but not whether a korban is due is liable -- so for the oath, unwitting of the korban suffices

answered_by.gloss_en: הא מני -- מונבז היא: the baraita is Munbaz's, and Abaye spoke for the Rabbis (= p_bar_shevua_kemunbaz)
